app.title: The Deepfake Detective Academy
app.hook: Some of the voices you hear today aren't real.

soundcheck.intro: Before we start: can you actually hear me? Everything after this is sound.
soundcheck.title: Sound check
soundcheck.body: Press the button. You should hear a short sentence. If you hear nothing, we'll help you fix it — nothing in this demo works without sound.
soundcheck.tipsTitle: No sound? Try these, in this order
soundcheck.tip1: Turn the volume up — on the device and in the browser.
soundcheck.tip2: Check the silent switch or Do Not Disturb; on a tablet it mutes everything.
soundcheck.tip3: If you're wearing headphones, check they're plugged in properly.
soundcheck.tip4: Then press the test sound once more — some browsers only allow sound after you tap.

setup.title: No audio samples yet
setup.body: The demo needs a set of audio samples first. Run these commands in the project folder:
setup.brokenTitle: The sample pack can't be read
setup.brokenBody: There is a manifest.json, but it doesn't match the format the app expects. Regenerate the pack:

miko.name: Miko the minion
miko.description: Miko understands words well, but sometimes falls for a fake voice.

echo.name: Agent Echo the detective
echo.description: Agent Echo hunts for the tiny sound clues that give a fake voice away.

b1.title: Inside the brain of a speech AI
b1.text: Hi! I'm Miko. I write down what I hear. Come and see how that works inside my head!

b2.title: Real or Fake?
b2.text: I'm Agent Echo, deepfake detective. Miko believes everything — I don't. Five voices await your verdict: real or fake?

b3.title: The compression machine
b3.text: Well done! But out there, phones squash voices flat. Look what that does to my evidence.

b4.title: The fake-voice factory
b4.text: Final mission. A voice you know is easy to believe — crooks abuse that. Now make a fake voice yourself and try to fool Miko.

station1.name: Inside the brain of a speech AI

stage0.miko: Sound is wobbling air! This is how a sentence feels in my ears. Press Listen.

stage1.miko: I turn the sound into a picture. Low at the bottom, high at the top. Bright means loud — can you find the loudest moment?

stage2.miko: Now I hunt for chunks of sound in the picture. I'm never sure — watch me guess!

stage3.miko: And then I glue the chunks together into words. Look, I'm writing along!

station1.waveLabel: The shape of the sound: tall means loud, flat means quiet
station1.specAlt: A sound picture: time runs left to right, low tones at the bottom, high tones at the top. Bright patches are loud.
station1.scrubLabel: Point at a moment in the sound picture
station1.scrubHint: Tap the picture, or use the arrow keys, to jump to that moment. Home and End go to the start and the end.
station1.peakPrompt: Point at the moment you think is the LOUDEST, then confirm.
station1.peakClose: Spot on! The loudest moment really is around {pct}% through — you can see it, and now you can hear it.
station1.peakFar: Not quite! The loudest moment is around {pct}% through. Look how much brighter the picture is there.
station1.peakExplain: That was measured from the sound itself, right here in your browser — not guessed by an AI. Bright in the picture really does mean loud.
station1.handoff: So that's how I hear! But whether a voice is real or fake? I can't tell. That's what Agent Echo is for…

station2.name: Real or Fake?
station2.echoPrompt: Listen closely. Is this a real human — or a computer?
station2.prompt1: Case one, an easy one. Listen closely: real or fake?
station2.prompt2: Case two. Mind the breath, slips and hiss…
station2.prompt3: Case three. The fake voices keep getting better…
station2.prompt4: Case four. Even real detectives hesitate here.
station2.prompt5: The last case. This one nearly fooled ME!
station2.specAlt: The sound picture for this case: time runs left to right, low tones at the bottom, high tones at the top.
station2.scoreHigh: Wow, you have detective ears! But out there my job is harder — come and see.
station2.scoreMid: Well done! Even real detectives hesitate sometimes. And it gets harder…
station2.scoreLow: Tricky, right? Fake voices have become very good. Come and see why…
station2.itWasReal: This voice was REAL — an ordinary human.
station2.itWasFake: This voice was FAKE — made by a computer.
station2.fooledStat: {pct}% of visitors fell for this one too!
station2.realExplanation: A real human. Hear the breath and the little slips? Real people are rarely tidy — that's a clue in this clip. It isn't a rule: a computer can add breaths too.
station2.realExplanationB: Real! Hear the room echo a little? Most real recordings aren't perfectly clean. Careful, though — a spotless recording can still be real.
station2.realExplanationC: A real human. The voice wobbles, hesitates and breathes. Many fake voices forget that. The very best ones don't.
station2.clueCaveat: Everything I circle is a clue about how THIS clip was made — never proof. The newest fake voices add breaths, hiss and room echo on purpose, and plenty of genuine recordings sound impossibly clean. A clue can point you somewhere. It can't settle it.
station2.echoDisclosure: And I should admit something: I'm not really listening. This demo was built with the answers written down beforehand, because we made the fake clips ourselves. There is no detector running on this screen — a real one would be unsure too.
station2.uncertainty: Nobody can be certain by ear — not you, not me, not the researchers who build these things. Fake voices improve every month, and the clues I showed you go away as soon as a message is compressed. So the real skill isn't hearing better. It's knowing what to do when you can't be sure — that's where we're heading.

station3.name: The compression machine
station3.echoIntro: Listen! The machine plays the same sentence four times — flatter every time. Watch the top of the picture…
station3.predictBody: The last setting is a really crackly voice message. Do you think Miko will still be able to write the sentence down?
station3.resultIdentical: Miko wrote down exactly the same sentence at the crackliest setting as at studio quality. The words survived the squashing completely.
station3.resultChanged: Miko still wrote a sentence at the crackliest setting, but not quite the same one. The words mostly survived; the details didn't.
station3.resultSilent: At the crackliest setting Miko got nothing at all. Even the words were squashed away.
station3.echoAfter: That's the catch. The words come through — but the evidence I look for lives at the top of the picture, and compression throws that away first. Which is exactly why crooks send voice messages.
station3.tryAll: Listen to all four settings first
station3.specAlt: The sound picture at the {level} setting.
station3.mikoHearsNothing: …almost nothing any more. The sound is too squashed!

station4.name: The fake-voice factory
station4.pickSentence: What should the fake voice say? Pick a sentence.
station4.mikoHeard: Miko is listening to the message
station4.mikoVerdict: Sounds fine to me! Message received.
station4.echoAlert: ALARM! This voice came out of a computer. I can see it in the picture right away!
station4.echoDisclosure: Well — "right away" is a bit much. I know this one is fake because you just built it in the machine, and the demo was made with that written down. Nothing on this screen is analysing the sound.
station4.noClueDescription: This sound picture has no single spot to point at — which happens with good fakes.
station4.lesson: Miko understood every word — but he couldn't hear it was fake. That's why you need both: a listener and a detective.
station4.scamTip: Real scammers do this too: they call parents with a fake voice of their child. Not sure? Hang up and call back on the number you already have.

final.intro: One last mission — and it's the one that matters outside this room.
final.title: A voice you know asks for money
final.body: It's late. A voice message arrives from someone you know well. It asks for money, right now. Real scammers usually add "don't tell anyone yet" — so that you don't check.
final.question: What do you do?

option.send: Send the money straight away — that really is their voice.
option.reply: Reply to that same message and ask something only they would know.
option.callback: Call the number you already have saved, and ask them yourself.
option.unsure: I honestly don't know — I'd freeze.

why.send: That's exactly what the scam is built for. A voice you love is very hard to doubt, and by the time you hear the real story the money is gone. The voice being right tells you nothing — a few seconds of speech is enough to copy it.
why.reply: This one feels like checking, and it isn't. Whoever sent that message is the very thing you're unsure about, so their answer proves nothing. A fake voice can answer questions too, and someone holding a stolen phone can answer personal ones. Check on a channel YOU picked, not the one they picked.
why.callback: Exactly right. Notice what you didn't have to do: spot anything. Calling back on a number you already had reaches the real person however good the fake was — which is why it still works when your ears have been fooled.
why.unsure: That's an honest answer, and it's where most people are. Here's the good news: you don't have to know. Do the same thing you'd do if you were certain it was fake — hang up and call back on the number you already have. If it turns out to be real, nothing is lost.

final.takeaway: You can't win this by listening harder. Check on a channel you chose yourself.

station5.name: Detective Diploma
station5.title: Detective Diploma
station5.hardest: The hardest case fooled {pct}% of everyone!
station5.verifyCrowd: {pct}% chose to call back and check.
station5.echoOutro: Well done, detective! The first one matters most:
station5.tip1: Does a familiar voice ask for money or a secret? Hang up and call back on the number you already have. That works even when the fake is perfect.
station5.tip2: Breath, hiss and little mistakes can be clues — but they're never proof. The best fakes have them too.
station5.tip3: Clever people get fooled too. Checking is smart, not silly.

clue.tier1: Hear how smooth this voice is? Look in the box: barely any wobble. That's my clue here — most real voices tremble a little. Newer fake ones can tremble too.
clue.tier2: Look in the box: empty and silent. No breath, no hiss. That's what tipped me off in this clip — though a cleaned-up real recording can look just as bare.
clue.tier3: Almost real! But the stripes in the box run very straight and even. That's a clue in this one. A straight stripe on its own never decides it.
clue.tier4: Well made — look how silent it goes between the words. That's the clue I used. A quiet room can do the same thing to a real recording.
clue.tier5: Even I looked twice. In the box: nothing messy, nothing human. A clue, not a verdict — this is roughly where my eyes stop being useful.
clue.smoothHarmonics: Look how smooth and even these stripes are. A real voice usually wobbles a little, so this is worth a second look — but "too smooth" is a hint, not an answer.
clue.noBreath: Where's the breath? People usually breathe in before they speak, and this voice just starts. Suspicious — although plenty of real clips get trimmed right up to the first word.
clue.hfCutoff: Look at the top: the high sounds stop suddenly, like there's a lid on them. That happens with some fakes — and with every phone call, which is why this clue disappears in mission 3.
clue.tooClean: This one was hard! No lip smacks, no hiss, no room echo. Too clean is a clue — a studio microphone can be too clean as well.
